name: Tract (Tract Capital Management portfolio company)
headquarters: Denver, Colorado, USA (3200 Cherry Creek South Drive, Suite 700 — the company's largest land position is in Storey and Lyon counties, Nevada)
employees: Not disclosed; LinkedIn lists about 80 employees (September 2026) and the team page names 60 people including a five-person Tract Europe group; the company said 'over 50' in May 2024
summary:
BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT: Tract is the horizontal half of a two-platform Denver asset manager — it buys, zones, entitles and services master-planned 'technology parks' and sells the shovel-ready parcels as a product, while its sister platform Fleet Data Centers builds single-tenant turnkey campuses on Tract land — and after four years and roughly 21,000 entitled acres the only transactions on the public record are Fleet's own two Storey County campuses, financed by USD 8.4 billion of high-yield notes against 197-month leases to an unnamed AA- tenant that Bloomberg identifies as Nvidia; whether a third-party operator ever buys a Tract parcel, and whether NV Energy's July 2026 lawsuit and the pending PUCN decisions on Tract's temporary gas plants leave the Nevada parks powered on their stated dates, are the two facts that decide the model.

BACKGROUND. Founded in 2022 by Grant van Rooyen, the founder of Cologix, as a portfolio company of Tract Capital Management (Denver; about USD 6 billion of assets under management per Bloomberg), Tract describes itself as 'a horizontal developer of master-planned data center parks' that pre-positions 'power, fiber, zoning, and entitlements' so that hyperscale and wholesale developers can 'drive capacity to market with speed and certainty'. Its projects page lists 14 parks totalling 21,078 acres and 18,695 MW across Nevada (five parks, 12,390 acres), Texas (three), Utah (two), Arizona, Iowa, Illinois and Virginia, and the company claims 'over 25GW of planned capacity and over 25,000 acres of land under control'. Institutional backers named by Data Center Frontier are Berkshire Partners (2023), Permira (June 2024), PSP Partners, S2G Ventures and Columbia Capital; the company itself names none. The record since 2024 is one of entitlement wins and losses in roughly equal measure: Hanover, Buckeye, Altoona, Lyon County and Morris (with a FERC-approved ComEd transmission security agreement) approved; Chesterfield withdrawn, Mooresville withdrawn, Hanover's second park rejected 4–3 in May 2026; a summary-judgment win over Switch's colocation covenant at the Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center in October 2025; and, since July 2026, a Washoe County suit by NV Energy to keep Tract's power-supply obligations before the utility commission rather than an arbitrator. Per company pages (read via Wayback captures — the live site blocks automated fetches), Fleet releases, PUCN dockets and the cited press.
ecosystemRole: The developer's developer: where Compass, EdgeCore and PowerHouse build or lease buildings, Tract sells the powered, permitted ground beneath them and leaves the vertical work to others — including its own affiliate Fleet, whose first two campuses sit on Tract parcels at the Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center. In this corpus it is a neighbour and rival of Vantage, EdgeCore, PowerHouse and Switch at TRIC (Switch is also its litigant), of Prime Data Centers and PowerHouse in Caldwell County, Texas, and of Meta, Google and QTS at Eagle Mountain; a Dominion Energy, ComEd, NV Energy, APS, Rocky Mountain Power, Bluebonnet and LCRA large-load customer; and, through Fleet, the reported landlord of Nvidia's first owned-lease campus.

productsAndServices.name: Master-planned technology parks — shovel-ready, powered, entitled parcels sold as a product (the core business)
productsAndServices.description: Tract 'acquires, zones, entitles, and develops master-planned technology campuses to provide Data Center end-users with speed and certainty' and sells 'shovel-ready development sites … as a product'; its What We Do page says it 'saves time for hyperscalers and data center developers' by 'acquiring and conditioning land specifically for data center construction and commissioning', and its Approach page frames the sale as 'When Cloud and Wholesale Data Centers invest in a Tract-owned parcel'. The horizontal scope at Peru Shelf was 'NV Energy switch stations, new access roads, and wet utility infrastructure'; per-site preparation spend is reported at USD 50–100 million (Richmond BizSense, Muskin Elam) or USD 100–150 million (Bisnow). The projects page (February 2026 capture) lists 14 parks, 21,078 acres and 18,695 MW, every one labelled 'Owned & In Development'; the company claims 'over 25GW of planned capacity and over 25,000 acres of land under control across the country, including campuses exceeding 1,000 acres and 1GW in each of Arizona, Iowa, Nevada, Texas, Utah and Virginia' (January 2026).
highlights: What a Tract parcel comes with, in the company's park-page vocabulary: by-right data-center zoning (Buckeye, Peru Shelf, Peru Ridge, Pole Canyon, Pony Express, Hanover), a development agreement (Altoona, Sapphire, Caldwell, Buckeye), a reserved water allocation (Altoona 588,000 gallons a day), an on-site or planned substation (South Valley 525/345 kV; Hanover up to eight Dominion substations; Caldwell a Bluebonnet/LCRA substation scaling to 1.6 GW), a stated energisation date (Peru Shelf February 2027; South Valley September 2027; Caldwell, Medina and Morris 2028) and parcel sizes from 40 to 1,200 acres.

No third-party parcel sale with a named buyer or price appears on any company page or in any fetched article; the only disclosed transactions are intra-group — Fleet Data Centers I subsidiaries bought a 252-acre and a 517-acre Storey County property from Tract-sponsored funds (Kirkland & Ellis, 2 March 2026: 'lease and purchase and sale of real property'). Richmond BizSense (2025) and the Eagle Mountain economic-development office (2024) describe the model as selling or leasing sites 'to other data center developers'; whether that has happened is the collection gap at the centre of this dossier.

Entitlement record: approvals at Hanover (May 2024, unanimous), Buckeye (August 2024, unanimous, with a development agreement reimbursing up to USD 50 million once the city collects USD 60 million), Lyon County (2025 rezoning and development agreement), Altoona (annexation, rezoning and development agreement), Farmington, Minnesota (final plat and PUD, November 2024) and Morris (fully zoned at purchase); losses at Chesterfield, Virginia (744 acres, planning commission denial recommended 17 June 2025, withdrawn 2 July), Mooresville, North Carolina (400 acres, withdrawn 13 August 2025 after opposition) and Hanover's Mountain Road Technology Park (about 430 acres, rejected 4–3 on 27 May 2026); Goochland, Virginia (870 acres, 900 MW) was in pre-application in July 2026.

The renewable pre-position: an exclusive collaboration with Silicon Ranch (January 2024) for more than 500 MW of owned solar and storage 'married to the data center land' in Nevada and Utah; the Approach page still cites 'a leading solar developer'.

Portfolio counters over time: 'more than 20,000 acres' (April 2024), 'over 23,000' (August 2024), 'over 25,000' (January 2026); Storey and Lyon County holdings 'over 12,500 acres' (September 2025) or '12,000 acres' (KOLO, May 2026). The counter is acreage under control, not acreage sold.
productsAndServices.positioning: Tract names no competitor. It is described alongside Vantage, EdgeCore, Novva, Switch, Google and Apple as a TRIC neighbour (Data Center Frontier), beside Prime Data Centers' campus 'across the street' in Caldwell County (Muskin Elam) and beside Chirisa, AREP/PowerHouse and Torch Clean Energy in Virginia (Bisnow). Its differentiation claim is the product itself — a parcel with power, water, fibre and zoning already in place — and the scale of the land bank; its exposure is that every other party in the chain (utility, county, tenant) decides when the parcel is worth paying for.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Sale of entitled parcels to data-center developers (the stated model); intra-group sale and ground lease to Fleet Data Centers' project companies (the only recorded transactions); development agreements and municipal reimbursements.
targetSegments: Hyperscalers (the company names Microsoft, Nvidia, Amazon and Meta as the market it serves, none as a customer)
Its own affiliate Fleet Data Centers
productsAndServices.roadmap: Peru Shelf energisation February 2027; South Valley September 2027 (construction power 2025); Caldwell first 250 MW Q1 2028 (substation to 1.6 GW); Medina mid-2028; Morris June 2028 with 1 GW by 2032; Hanover 2028 (bridging power 'as early as 2026'); Eagle Mountain more than 400 MW by 2028. Tract Europe 'actively engaged … to identify, entitle & proactively invest in the next generation of build-ready sites' (2026) with no European site listed.

productsAndServices.name: The Nevada parks — Peru Shelf, Peru Ridge, South Valley, Virginia Highlands and Sapphire (12,390 acres, 5,455 MW on the projects page)
productsAndServices.category: Master-planned parks, Storey and Lyon counties
productsAndServices.description: Tract's largest position began with about 2,200 acres bought from Blockchains LLC in 2023 with 1,100 acre-feet of water rights (Peru Shelf, 686 acres, up to 810 MW; South Valley, 1,500 acres, 1,200 MW), added 517 acres inside the Tahoe-Reno Industrial Center in February 2024 (Peru Ridge, 230 MW, with a pre-graded pad), 8,590 acres between TRIC and the Virginia City Highlands in June 2024 (Virginia Highlands, 2,500 MW, 11 parcels of 250–1,200 acres) and about 1,060 acres at Silver Springs in Lyon County in September 2025 (Sapphire, 700 MW under utility study, 'up to 1.6 gigawatts'). Peru Shelf broke ground on 30 April 2024 (Westex Geotechnical; F&P Construction) with 'NV Energy switch stations' in scope and 'initial power delivery in late 2026 or early 2027', now stated as 'Site energization February 2027, construction power available immediately'; South Valley's page lists an 'On-Site 525/345 kV Substation' and 'Site energization September 2027'. NV Energy's own account (NewsData, August 2026) is that Tract 'plans to build at least five data centers with a combined load of nearly 5.5 GW in the state'.
highlights: The two campuses actually under construction are Fleet's: SV RNO Property Owner I, LLC (252 acres, South Valley) and PR RNO Property Owner I, LLC (517 acres — the Peru Ridge acreage) are each building a '230 MW utility / 200 MW IT' turnkey data center and substation, '100% leased to a AA- investment grade rated tenant with a market cap in excess of $3 trillion' on 197-month triple-net leases, financed by USD 3.8 billion of 5.875% notes due 2031 (priced 13 February 2026) and USD 4.6 billion of 6.500% notes due 2031 (closed 1 May 2026). Bloomberg identifies the tenant as Nvidia with an initial term of about 16 years and two 10-year options; Fleet has not confirmed. The groundbreaking with Governor Lombardo on 20 May 2026 was reported as a USD 4.6 billion, 2-million-square-foot build with 1,500 peak construction jobs.

Power before the substation: the two Fleet SPVs applied to the PUCN on 20 April 2026 for temporary gas plants — 144 MW at South Valley (docket 26-04026) and 218 MW at Peru Ridge (26-04027), the 'Peru Ridge Self-Generation Project' — with a decision scheduled for 8 September 2026; SV RNO applied on 7 April for a new 345 kV substation and four 345 kV lines (26-04007); NV Energy filed a large-load electric service agreement with both SPVs on 29 May (26-05027); Reno Power NR 1 noticed an approximately 88.6-mile 525 kV transmission loop (26-02021) and petitioned for an advisory opinion on Rule 9 (25-09008); Storey County's planning commission recommended Tract's six-mile 345 kV line to a new NV Energy 'Mackay' substation on 4 September 2025.

The utility dispute: under June 2024 agreements with Tract subsidiary Reno Power, Tract demanded arbitration on 16 June 2026; NV Energy sued Tract Capital Management in Washoe County on 24 July 2026 (CV26-02142) to keep supply adequacy, cost allocation and resource-plan treatment before the PUCN, saying Tract 'wants NV Energy to reserve and provide enormous amounts of power for Tract's private development while shifting the infrastructure and energy costs to Nevada families'; Tract says it has spent 'more than $127 million' on its obligations and that NV Energy is demanding it commit 'USD 1 billion in network infrastructure upgrades for the benefit of all NV Energy customers'.

The covenant fight: Switch sued in August 2023 over a 2015 TRIC covenant barring multi-tenant colocation on Peru Shelf ('only 5% of Tract's total Reno portfolio'); Judge Woodbury granted Switch a preliminary injunction on a relocated easement in July 2025, then summary judgment to Tract on the covenant on 29 September 2025 (final judgment October) confirming 'Tract's right to horizontally prepare the Peru Shelf for the development by others of any type of data center that is not a multi-tenant data center facility'; the easement trial set for March 2026 has no reported outcome.
productsAndServices.positioning: TRIC is the most crowded powered-land market in the corpus — Vantage NV1 (224 MW), EdgeCore (216 MW), Novva, PowerHouse, Switch, Google and Apple — and Tract holds the largest raw acreage by a wide margin; its 5.5 GW of stated load is, per NV Energy, about a third of the utility's generating capacity, which is the arithmetic behind the lawsuit.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Parcels held by Tract-sponsored funds ('Tract I'); the two active campuses sold and ground-leased to Fleet's project SPVs; power contracted through Reno Power NR 1 and the SPVs with NV Energy (Sierra Pacific Power).
targetSegments: Non-multi-tenant data centers on Peru Shelf (covenant)
productsAndServices.roadmap: PUCN decision on the temporary gas plants 8 September 2026; Fleet campus operations targeted Q3 2027 per trade press; Peru Shelf February 2027 and South Valley September 2027 energisation; Sapphire 700 MW study; 525 kV loop federal application.

productsAndServices.name: The Sun Belt and Midwest parks — Texas, Arizona, Utah, Iowa, Illinois, Virginia and the Minnesota pipeline
productsAndServices.category: Master-planned parks outside Nevada (8,688 acres, 13,240 MW on the projects page)
productsAndServices.description: Caldwell Valley, Texas ('Project Snow'): 1,515 acres closed 7 May 2025 after '18 months' of pre-work with a Bluebonnet Electric Cooperative facility design agreement for 360 MW in 2028, plus 1,458 acres in January 2026 for about 2,973 acres and 'more than 4 GW', a Bluebonnet/LCRA on-site substation 'capable of scaling to 1.6GW' with 'the first 250MW of capacity contracted for delivery in the first quarter of 2028', 345 kV lines and the Kinder Morgan Permian Highway pipeline, and 'plans for onsite power generation that will become grid connected'; Medina (265 acres, 500 MW, Medina Electric Cooperative, mid-2028, adjacent to Microsoft's Castroville campus) and Applewhite in south San Antonio (339 acres, 720 MW design). Buckeye, Arizona: 2,069 acres bought in August 2024 for USD 136 million from Cipriani Holdings, 'up to 20 million square feet … as many as 40 individual data centers', up to 1.8 GW with APS, 22 by-right parcels of 44–242 acres, a development agreement approved unanimously — still 'planned or proposed' in May 2026. Eagle Mountain, Utah: 668 acres (January 2024) inside the RTI overlay with by-right use and 'more than 400 megawatts' from Rocky Mountain Power by 2028 (Pole Canyon 844 acres/1,700 MW; Pony Express 225 acres/120 MW next to Meta, Google and QTS). Altoona, Iowa: 453 acres (September 2025) with annexation, rezoning, a development agreement and a 588,000-gallon-a-day water reservation, 'over 1GW'. Morris, Illinois: 343 acres (January 2026, about USD 51.5 million from a Clarius Partners affiliate) with a ComEd transmission security agreement for 1 GW approved by FERC in April 2026, first power June 2028 and full ramp by 2032. Hanover, Virginia: 1,200 acres (May 2024, about USD 32.7 million) approved unanimously for up to 2.4 GW across eight Dominion substations, long-lead equipment ordered, bridging power 'as early as 2026', energisation 2028.
highlights: Texas is the largest non-Nevada position and the one with a contracted first block (250 MW, Q1 2028) — but also the site of a county whose commissioners suspended data-center abatements in August 2026 and where Prime Data Centers' USD 4 billion campus sits 'across the street'.

Morris is the only park with a FERC-accepted utility contract: the ComEd TSA (counterparty Grundy County Power NR I, LLC) carries 'committed revenue contributions, minimum usage commitments, and shortfall payments for underperformance' — the same instrument that ComEd cancelled on PowerHouse's Joliet campus in July 2026.

Virginia is where the model has lost most often: Chesterfield's 744 acres withdrawn (July 2025) under a county that now requires conditional-use permits and has 'signaled an end to data center approvals'; Hanover's second park rejected 4–3 (May 2026) despite a planning-commission 6–1 recommendation, a USD 15 million water pledge and a claimed USD 901 million of property tax over twenty years; Goochland's 870 acres opposed at pre-application (July 2026).

The Minnesota and Carolina pipeline is press-only: Farmington (343 acres including a golf course, final plat approved November 2024), Rosemount (447 acres, environmental review), Cannon Falls (about 250 acres, 'USD 30 billion over 20 years', Dakota Electric) and the withdrawn Mooresville park on Earnhardt family land — none appears on the company's projects page.
productsAndServices.positioning: Every park is sold on the same four claims — by-right zoning, a development agreement, a utility date and a water reservation — and priced against the county's willingness to grant them; the Buckeye reimbursement (USD 50 million after USD 60 million of city revenue) and the Caldwell arrangement ('no county tax incentives requested') show two ends of that trade.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Fee-simple land held by Tract entities (Grundy County Power NR I in Illinois; Caldwell parcels; Buckeye), with utility contracts signed in Tract's name ahead of any buyer.
targetSegments: Hyperscale and wholesale developers in secondary markets with power (Phoenix West Valley, Central Texas, Des Moines, Chicago exurbs, Richmond)
productsAndServices.roadmap: Caldwell 250 MW Q1 2028 and 1.6 GW substation; Morris June 2028 to 1 GW by 2032; Hanover 2028; Eagle Mountain 2028; Buckeye and Altoona undated; Goochland conditional-use application pending; Cannon Falls vote and 'summer 2026' construction hope unconfirmed.

productsAndServices.name: Fleet Data Centers — the vertical sister platform (500 MW+ single-user campuses on Tract land)
productsAndServices.category: Affiliate: build-to-suit mega-campus developer and operator
productsAndServices.description: Tract Capital introduced Fleet Data Centers on 8 January 2025 as 'the mega-campus vertical development strategy' beside Tract's 'horizontal powered land strategy': 'a developer and operator of mega-scale, single-user data center campuses' targeting '500 MW+ build-to-suit megacampuses for single-user customers', led by President Chris Vonderhaar (ex-Google Cloud vice president and AWS data-center executive) with Grant van Rooyen as executive chairman. Its first fund, Fleet Data Centers I, LP, holds the two Storey County project companies; the USD 4.6 billion closing release says proceeds also 'reimburse the Issuer's sponsor for prior equity contributions used to fund acquisition of property for the Project'.
highlights: Bond terms as released: USD 3.8 billion 5.875% senior secured notes due 1 March 2031 (SV RNO Property Owner I; 144A/Reg S; 2.5% annual amortisation; first-priority liens on the issuer's assets and the equity of SV RNO HoldCo) and USD 4.6 billion 6.500% notes due 1 May 2031 (PR RNO Property Owner I; priced at 99 to yield 6.74% per Bloomberg Law). Bloomberg: JPMorgan lead and Morgan Stanley co-manager on the first deal; Fleet I equity 'about USD 620 million'; Fleet calls the February issue 'the highest-rated, largest issuance, highest loan-to-cost, and tightest pricing for any single data center high-yield bond project financing to date' (Baxtel).

Why Fleet exists, in FOSS Force's account of the launch: 'Leasing model preferred over sales' — the vertical arm captures the lease the horizontal arm cannot, and the Nevada campuses were chosen for 'earliest utility power delivery'.

Fleet's tenant is the corpus's most valuable unnamed counterparty: 'AA- investment grade rated tenant with a market cap in excess of $3 trillion' in every release; Nvidia per Bloomberg (February and April 2026); Baxtel lists Nvidia, Alphabet, Apple and Microsoft as the candidates the description fits.
productsAndServices.positioning: Fleet competes with EdgeCore, Vantage and the F7 landlords for single-tenant hyperscale leases; its advantage is that its landlord already owns the powered ground.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Project-company leases (197-month triple-net) financed with senior secured notes; sponsor equity from Fleet Data Centers I, LP.
productsAndServices.roadmap: Both Storey County campuses under construction from May 2026; operations targeted 2027; further Fleet campuses unannounced.

productsAndServices.name: Energy and grid services around the parks — utility contracts, temporary generation, renewables and a gas desk
productsAndServices.category: Power pre-positioning (the part of the product the utility controls)
productsAndServices.description: Tract's team page lists a Chief Energy Officer (2024), an SVP Utility Development who founded Dominion's data-center services group, an SVP Energy Development from Calpine and Competitive Power Ventures, a VP Regulatory Affairs, a VP Energy Procurement 'responsible for ensuring the procurement of reliable, cost-effective supply to meet the needs of data centers' power generation facilities', a Manager of Gas Supply 'supporting the company's natural gas strategy', and transmission-planning directors from Invenergy and Recurrent. The instruments on the record: the ComEd transmission security agreement (Morris, FERC-approved); the Bluebonnet facility design agreement and LCRA substation (Caldwell); Dominion's eight-substation plan (Hanover); the June 2024 NV Energy agreements with Reno Power; the Silicon Ranch solar-and-storage collaboration (Nevada and Utah); and, in 2026, the two temporary gas plants (144 MW and 218 MW) Fleet's SPVs asked the PUCN to permit while the grid connection is built.
highlights: The gas plants are the model's stress point: the Nevada Independent reported that the private plants 'would skirt' the state's renewable standard, the Sierra Club opposed them, and the PUCN's decision is scheduled for 8 September 2026 — three days after this dossier.
Caldwell's January 2026 release says Tract 'has initiated plans for onsite power generation that will become grid connected' — the Panhandle/Fermi pattern arriving at the powered-land developer.
productsAndServices.positioning: Powered land is only powered when the utility agrees; Tract's 2026 record — a FERC-approved TSA in Illinois, a lawsuit in Nevada — shows both outcomes on the same product.
productsAndServices.soldThrough: Utility agreements held by Tract or Fleet entities; bridging generation permitted to the project SPVs.
targetSegments: Parcel buyers and Fleet tenants who need a dated power supply
productsAndServices.roadmap: PUCN gas-plant decision 8 September 2026; NV Energy litigation and arbitration; Silicon Ranch projects undated.

relationships.note: Adverse litigant: Switch sued Tract's Storey County entity in 2023 to enforce a 2015 TRIC covenant barring multi-tenant colocation on Peru Shelf; Tract won summary judgment on the covenant in October 2025 while Switch holds a preliminary injunction on a relocated easement.
relationships.context: Tract's 13 October 2025 release reports the final judgment confirming its right to prepare Peru Shelf for 'any type of data center that is not a multi-tenant data center facility' and says the covenant affects 'only 5% of Tract's total Reno portfolio'; the Nevada Independent's series covers Switch's July 2025 injunction preserving a 100-foot easement and the March 2026 easement trial, whose outcome is not on the record. Tract's counterclaims accuse Switch, Rob Roy, DigitalBridge and Marc Ganzi of interference. Switch is also a TRIC neighbour and, at its Citadel campus, the incumbent the covenant was written to protect.

relationships.note: Prime Data Centers' USD 4 billion Lockhart campus sits 'across the street' from Tract's Caldwell Valley park in Caldwell County, Texas — the two developers compete for the same Bluebonnet-served hyperscale tenants.

policyExposure.regime: Nevada large-load service and cost allocation — NV Energy v. Tract Capital Management (Washoe County CV26-02142) and PUCN dockets
policyExposure.exposure: NV Energy sued on 24 July 2026 to keep power-supply adequacy, large-load cost allocation and resource-plan treatment of Tract's loads before the PUCN rather than the arbitrator Tract invoked on 16 June under June 2024 agreements with subsidiary Reno Power; the utility describes Tract's plan as 'at least five data centers with a combined load of nearly 5.5 GW' and seeks USD 1 billion of network upgrades; Tract says it has spent more than USD 127 million on its obligations. NV Energy's large-load electric service agreement with the two Fleet SPVs (26-05027) and the temporary gas plant permits (26-04026, 26-04027; decision 8 September 2026) sit in the same commission.
policyExposure.mitigation: Tract's stated position is that the June 2024 contracts govern and that it 'never asked or expected for our costs to be subsidized by others'; the Fleet SPVs applied for 362 MW of temporary on-site gas generation and a new 345 kV substation so the first campuses do not wait on the dispute.

policyExposure.exposure: The Morris park's 1 GW depends on a ComEd transmission security agreement with Grundy County Power NR I, LLC that FERC approved in April 2026; the agreement carries 'committed revenue contributions, minimum usage commitments, and shortfall payments for underperformance', and ComEd cancelled the same class of agreement on PowerHouse's Joliet campus in July 2026 over deposit timing.

policyExposure.exposure: The product is the entitlement, so every park is a vote: approvals at Hanover (2024), Buckeye (2024), Farmington (2024), Lyon County (2025), Altoona (2025) and Morris; defeats at Chesterfield (withdrawn July 2025; the county now requires conditional-use permits from 1 January 2026 and 'signaled an end to data center approvals' in August 2026), Mooresville (withdrawn August 2025) and Hanover's Mountain Road park (rejected 4–3, May 2026); Goochland pending. strategyRead: (High confidence) We assess that Tract's product — an entitled, powered parcel sold to another developer — has not yet been sold to anyone outside the group: the only recorded transactions are the two Storey County parcels bought by Fleet's project companies from Tract-sponsored funds. Basis: no company page or fetched article names a third-party buyer or price across four years and fourteen parks; Kirkland & Ellis's March 2026 release describes the Fleet purchase-and-sale; Fleet was launched in January 2025 with a 'leasing model preferred over sales'. Collection gap: unreported private sales are possible; none is visible.

(High confidence) We assess that the value the market has priced is the affiliate's, not Tract's: USD 8.4 billion of five-year secured notes at 5.875–6.5% against two 197-month leases to a tenant Bloomberg names as Nvidia, with about USD 620 million of sponsor equity. The horizontal platform's economics — land bought at USD 51,000–66,000 an acre in Morris and Buckeye, USD 50–150 million of infrastructure per park — are invisible in every disclosure. Basis: Fleet's releases and the Bloomberg bond reporting; the disclosed land prices.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the Nevada position, 12,000 acres and 5.5 GW of stated load, is now contingent on a utility dispute the company cannot control: NV Energy's July 2026 suit, the USD 1 billion network-upgrade demand and the 8 September 2026 PUCN decision on 362 MW of temporary gas generation together decide whether 'Site energization February 2027' at Peru Shelf and 'September 2027' at South Valley hold. Basis: NewsData, CBS and the Nevada Independent on the suit; the PUCN docket index; the park pages. Indicator: the PUCN order and any settlement or ruling on the arbitration.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the entitlement product succeeds where a county wants growth and fails where residents organise, and that the ratio is roughly even: six approvals against three losses since 2024, with Virginia the weakest market (one approval, two withdrawals or rejections, one contested pre-application). Basis: the county records and local press listed in Policy Exposure; the company's own consent offers (water pledges, road cash, no-incentive stances, a property-values white paper) show it pricing consent as a cost line.

(Moderate confidence) We assess that the 2024 executive build-out has partly unwound: the CFO, Chief Energy Officer, Chief Innovation Officer and Head of Capital Formation hired in January–February 2024 are absent from the 2026 team page, the founder moved from CEO to Executive Chairman, and the former CIO is now President. Basis: the who-we-are page against the 2024 releases and Equilar's change log; no departure was announced, so the reading is inference from absence. What it suggests: a platform that pivoted from raising a fund to executing two campuses through Fleet.

(Low confidence) We assess that Tract's 2026 moves toward on-site generation — the Fleet gas plants in Nevada, 'onsite power generation that will become grid connected' at Caldwell, a gas-supply desk on the team page — are the beginning of a shift from powered land to power-generating land, which would put it in Fermi America's and Intersect Power's business rather than PowerHouse's. Basis: the PUCN applications, the January 2026 Caldwell release and the team roster; nothing built.

Collection gap: the live tract.com, tractcapital.com and fleetdatacenters.com sites block automated fetches, so every company page was read from Wayback captures dated between October 2025 and August 2026; headcount, the sellers and prices of the Nevada parcels, the outcome of the March 2026 easement trial, any refiling in Chesterfield and the status of the Minnesota parks are unknown. INDICATORS TO WATCH: 8 September 2026 — PUCN decision on dockets 26-04026 and 26-04027; the Washoe County case and arbitration; any third-party parcel sale with a named buyer; Fleet's tenant confirmation or a third Fleet campus; the Goochland application; Peru Shelf's February 2027 energisation.
